opportunities.title: Front door rebuild: own-domain site with tap-to-call, a real consultation request form, hours, and schema an AI assistant can read and book from
opportunities.problem: The firm's entire web presence is one free Weebly page last modified in 2015 whose only call to action does not work: the hero button 'CALL NOW (732) 766-5703' is an anchor with href="javascript:;", there is no tel: link, no form, no email, no hours and no booking. A DWI defendant searching at 11pm must memorise a number from the page text and dial it manually, and no assistant (Siri, ChatGPT, Google) can extract hours, a service area or a booking path because there is no meta description and no JSON-LD.
evidence: Hero 'CALL NOW (732) 766-5703' is an anchor with href="javascript:;" (non-functional) and the page has no tel: link — https://hugheslaw.weebly.com/
No contact form, email address, chat or online scheduler anywhere; phone (732) 766-5703 is the only channel and appears four times as plain text — https://hugheslaw.weebly.com/
Sitemap contains exactly one URL (index.html) with lastmod 2015-05-21, served from a free Weebly subdomain — https://hugheslaw.weebly.com/sitemap.xml
No meta description, no JSON-LD/schema markup; title is a run-on of name, titles and phone with no practice area or town — https://hugheslaw.weebly.com/
No business hours published on the site or on the Lawyers.com profile — https://www.lawyers.com/east-brunswick/new-jersey/mark-f-hughes-iii-esquire-17009746-f/
Third-party review of the same site records click_to_call=false, contact_form=false, findable=0 and bookable=0 — triage.json, website_review/agent_readiness
opportunities.agent_design: Capability G is a fixed asset first, agent second. (1) Four to six pages on an owned domain: DWI/Alcotest refusal, suspended/uninsured driving, CDS, theft/shoplifting, domestic-violence, juvenile — each naming the actual courts served in Middlesex and Monmouth counties, with real hours for both suites and a tel: link on every page. (2) Schema.org LegalService + Attorney + openingHoursSpecification + areaServed for the two offices, a meta description per page, and a plain-language answer block ('what happens after a DWI arrest in Middlesex County') so assistant crawlers can cite and route. (3) A consultation request form that writes to a shared inbox/spreadsheet with an acknowledgement SMS, because the attorney has no CRM. (4) A thin routing agent sits behind the form: classify the charge and county, extract court date if given, and queue the request with a suggested consult slot; the attorney approves every appointment and every reply before it is sent. No legal advice is generated by the agent — it captures facts and books time only. Sequence note: go-live is gated on confirming the attorney's current eligibility to practise (see opportunity 2); the build can proceed while that is resolved.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A Wix/Squarespace template can produce a prettier one-pager, and honestly that part is close to DIY — the defensible work here is the parts a template does not do: correct LegalService/Attorney schema across two offices, page structure and copy aimed at assistant-answerable queries, a form-to-inbox-to-acknowledgement chain with an SMS receipt, and measurement of whether calls actually arrive. A template also repeats the current failure mode, which is that the site was built once and abandoned; the agent layer is what keeps hours, courts and charge pages current.

impact_estimate.range: No revenue claim is made — there is no sourced figure for this firm's enquiry volume or fee per matter. The measurable, defensible saving is clerical re-work: roughly $3,000–$6,300 per year of legal-secretary time (2–4 hours/week at $30.30/hr median) currently spent answering and re-keying the same phone-only enquiries.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes the practice is live and taking matters; assumes 2–4 hrs/week of clerical intake handling, which is an inference from a phone-only channel with a published number repeated four times, not a measured figure. Median wage converted at 2,080 hrs/yr. The larger effect — after-hours calls that are currently lost outright — cannot be sized from any source in the profile and is deliberately excluded.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Two to four weeks: owned domain with three charge-specific pages plus a two-office contact page; tel: links and a working consultation form with SMS acknowledgement; LegalService/Attorney schema and per-page meta; hours published; a documented, measured baseline of form submissions and call attempts so the next phase has a number to beat. Deliverable is live and crawlable, not a mockup.

opportunities.title: Administrative-compliance and court-calendar agent: never miss an IOLTA/Client Protection Fund/CLE obligation or a municipal court date in two vicinages
opportunities.problem: The attorney appears on New Jersey's administrative ineligibility lists in 2024, in 2025 and again on the current 2026 Client Protection Fund list — and, notably, he does not appear on the March 31, 2026 notice of attorneys reinstated from the 2025 list. Those are administrative compliance failures (annual assessment, IOLTA, fee), not findings of misconduct, but a listed attorney is administratively ineligible to practise, which means no new matters and no point automating intake. Nothing on the site or in the firm's footprint shows any recurring deadline-tracking habit: no hours, no staff, no systems, one attorney covering court calendars in two counties.
evidence: 'Hughes, Mark Fabian', attorney ID 021041994, year admitted 1994, appears on the 2026 NJ Lawyers' Fund for Client Protection ineligible list (period ending November 09, 2026) — https://www.njcourts.gov/sites/default/files/attorneys/new-jersey-lawyers-fund-client-protection/ineliglist.pdf

Same attorney ID appears on the Supreme Court's IOLTA 2025 Ineligible List effective September 9, 2025, and on the 2024 IOLTA list — https://www.njcourts.gov/sites/default/files/notices/2025/09/n250910a.pdf

Inference from a source opened: the March 31, 2026 notice of attorneys reinstated from the 2025 Client Protection Fund list does not contain the name Hughes, so as of that date he had not been reinstated from the 2025 list — https://www.njcourts.gov/sites/default/files/notices/2026/03/n260401a.pdf

Administrative ineligibility means the attorney 'cannot currently practice' while listed, and the status is reinstated once requirements are met — https://www.njcourts.gov/host/attyapps/GoodStandingStatusDefinitions.pdf

One named attorney, no staff, paralegal or reception function anywhere on the site or directories, covering calendars in Middlesex and Monmouth counties — https://www.martindale.com/attorney/mark-fabian-hughes-iii-159927509/
opportunities.agent_design: A deadline-and-obligation agent with the same shape as a docketing clerk, deliberately narrow. (1) An obligations register built once from the NJ Courts notices: annual Client Protection Fund assessment, IOLTA compliance/reporting, annual attorney registration, CLE cycle, malpractice renewal — each with its statutory trigger date, a 60/30/7-day reminder ladder by email and SMS, and the exact portal URL and payment amount where published. (2) A document assembler that pre-fills the renewal/assessment paperwork with the attorney ID, admitted-year and firm details and drops a ready-to-sign PDF into a folder; the attorney signs and submits — the agent never files, never pays, never touches the trust account. (3) A court-calendar agent: the attorney pastes or forwards a municipal court notice or eCourts confirmation, the agent extracts date, court, county, charge and appearance type, writes it to one calendar, and produces a Monday-morning list of the week's appearances across both vicinages with conflicts flagged. (4) A monthly status check that opens the published ineligibility lists, searches for the attorney's name and flags any hit — no scraping of private systems, public PDFs only. Human approval: every reminder and every prepared document is reviewed before it leaves; nothing is auto-filed. This is the opportunity that must be sold first, because it is the precondition for anything else working.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A calendar reminder is DIY; the reliable version is not. It needs a register of state-specific obligations with the right trigger dates and portals, recurring monitoring of public ineligibility lists, pre-filled document assembly keyed to an attorney ID, conflict detection across two court calendars, and an audit trail showing what was flagged and when — because the consequence of a miss is loss of the ability to practise, and O*NET data show lawyers themselves rate 'consequence of error' as extremely serious in 50% of responses. A missed reminder in a personal calendar has no detection, no escalation and no record.

impact_estimate.range: Labour saved: roughly 15–40 hours a year of deadline tracking, form pre-filling and calendar entry, about $450–$1,200 at the $30.30/hr median legal-secretary rate. The material number is the downside it insures, and it is an inference, not a measurement: while administratively ineligible the attorney cannot take new matters, so one avoided lapse protects a whole year of intake rather than a few hours of typing.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes the firm currently handles these obligations ad hoc with no staff (inference from no staff listed and three consecutive years of listings). Hour estimate is a planning assumption, not sourced. Wage converted at 2,080 hrs/yr. No dollar value is placed on avoided ineligibility because the profile contains no case volume or fee data to multiply.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Two to four weeks: a documented obligations register with the next 12 months of dated reminders; the pre-filled PDF templates for the assessment and registration; a live public-list monitor that emails a flag when the attorney's name appears or disappears; court-date extraction working on ten real past notices; one consolidated calendar across both offices. If the attorney is currently listed, the first deliverable in week one is the exact remediation path and dates — that is the value in the room.

opportunities.title: After-hours DWI intake agent: answers the 11pm arrest call, collects charge/county/court date, books the free consultation, hands the attorney a brief
opportunities.problem: DWI and Alcotest refusal work generates calls at the moment of arrest — nights, weekends, from a holding cell or a spouse's phone — and this firm offers exactly one way in: a phone number printed as text, with no hours published, no voicemail-to-email, no form and no booking. With no staff and one attorney travelling between Middlesex and Monmouth court calendars, every unanswered ring is a matter that goes to whichever firm answers. The triage review scored the site findable=0, answerable=1, bookable=0.
evidence: Phone-only intake: 'Call (732) 766-5703' appears four times and is the sole call to action; no form, email, chat or scheduler — https://hugheslaw.weebly.com/

No business hours anywhere on the site or the Lawyers.com profile, despite a caseload whose trigger events (arrests, court dates) happen outside business hours — https://www.lawyers.com/east-brunswick/new-jersey/mark-f-hughes-iii-esquire-17009746-f/
Practice areas are DWI and refusal, suspended/uninsured driving, CDS, theft/shoplifting and disorderly persons — a high-frequency, first-contact-heavy caseload — https://hugheslaw.weebly.com/
Two offices in two counties with one attorney and no support staff, so calls compete directly with court appearances — https://www.martindale.com/attorney/mark-fabian-hughes-iii-159927509/

Automated legal-intake triage is technically feasible: an ensemble of inexpensive models with auto-generated follow-up questions reached 97.37% hits@2 in routing 419 real queries for a nonprofit lawyer referral service (conference paper, JURIX 2025, arXiv preprint) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07170

Field evidence from text-heavy service work: generative AI assistance raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average (34% for novice workers), in a study published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics (NBER working paper 31161) — https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161
opportunities.agent_design: An intake agent on two surfaces, SMS/web first and voice second. Triggers: an inbound call that goes unanswered after 3 rings, an SMS to the published number, or a form submission outside 9–6. Flow: (1) collect the minimum facts — name, callback number, county and court if known, charge as the caller understands it (DWI / refusal / suspended licence / CDS / other), arrest or court date, whether anyone is in custody; (2) answer only from an approved, attorney-written FAQ (what to bring, what the free consultation covers, what happens at a first appearance) and never on penalty, plea or strategy; (3) check the attorney's live calendar and offer two real consultation slots, confirming by SMS; (4) escalate anything involving custody, a same-day court date, a juvenile or domestic-violence allegation to the attorney by phone immediately, day or night; (5) deliver a one-page brief per enquiry to the attorney — caller, charge, county, court date, urgency flag — before the consult. Confidentiality: zero-retention model endpoints or a private deployment, since callers are describing pending criminal charges (N.J. RPC 1.6). Human approval: no fee quote, no engagement, no legal advice without the attorney; the agent books time and captures facts only. Hard dependency: this only goes live once the eligibility question in opportunity 2 is resolved, because an ineligible attorney cannot take the matters it would book.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: An answering service or a Squarespace form cannot classify a charge, recognise that 'they took my licence at the scene' needs a same-night callback, offer a real slot from a live calendar, and produce a structured brief; and a consumer chatbot is the wrong tool for a caller describing a criminal charge, given that general-purpose models hallucinate on verifiable legal questions roughly 58% of the time in one peer-reviewed measurement and that a preregistered evaluation of commercial legal RAG tools found 17–33% hallucination (working paper). Getting this right is retrieval restricted to attorney-approved content plus a hard no-advice boundary plus escalation rules — engineering and liability design, not a subscription.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 60–180 hours a year of the attorney's non-billable intake and call-handling time, worth about $4,700–$14,000 at the $77.6/hr NJ lawyer median — the labour value only. Additional matters captured from after-hours calls are the real prize but are excluded here because the profile has no enquiry volume or fee-per-matter data.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 5–15 hours/month of intake and follow-up handling by the attorney personally (inference: phone-only channel, no staff). Labour productivity uplift taken conservatively at the low end of the 14% average from the QJE/NBER support-work study, applied as an analogy to intake and routine client correspondence, not as a law-firm measurement. Lawyer median $161,430 converted at 2,080 hrs/yr. Zero revenue per new matter assumed, since no fee data exists.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Two to four weeks: after-hours web/SMS intake live with an attorney-approved FAQ bank of 15–20 answers; two-slot consultation booking into a real calendar; escalation routing for custody/same-day/juvenile/domestic-violence flags; a structured brief per enquiry; a two-week log of enquiries handled, after-hours volume and escalations so the go/no-go on voice can be made on data. Voice channel is phase two, not pilot scope.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (21/30): unusually well documented for a solo — the hero call button is literally dead (href="javascript:;"), there is no tel: link, no form, no hours and no booking on a single page untouched since 2015, and the attorney appears on NJ administrative ineligibility lists in 2024, 2025 and 2026 with no entry on the March 31, 2026 reinstatement notice. What caps it is that pain is proven at the front door and in compliance, not in revenue: no case volume, fee or enquiry data exists anywhere. Fit (17/20): the front-door rebuild is capability G, and both the deadline/docket clerk and the after-hours DWI intake are textbook A — plus a natural C component in the approved-answer bank and an F retainer to keep the site, hours and calendar current. No E: profile.json shows desk-and-courtroom work, leased suites, no fleet, inventory, shop floor or dock, and no avenues.json was supplied, so a physical/edge opportunity would be manufactured rather than evidenced. Ability to pay (6/20): solo practice, two small leased suites, a website abandoned for a decade, no staff, and a practice that may be barred from taking new matters right now — this is a candidate who may not be in a position to buy until the compliance issue is fixed, which is precisely why opportunity 2 comes with remediation work attached. Ease (12/15): the site build and the deadline register are short, well-bounded jobs with no client data in scope, and the attorney is the sole decision maker so there is no procurement; marks off because a pilot cannot be judged on revenue while the practice is administratively restricted. Strategic (12/15): the pattern — one-page builder site, phone-only intake, night-time DWI calls, no reviews, recurring state compliance listings — repeats across thousands of New Jersey solo criminal/DWI practices, so a fixed front-door-plus-intake-plus-deadline product is highly reusable; marks off only because the compliance element is state-specific and the buyer segment is price-sensitive. BOTTOM LINE: do not lead with a large build. Lead with the eligibility remediation and deadline register, prove value in two weeks, and let the front-door rebuild and intake agent follow once the attorney can take matters again.

best_evidence_signal: The only conversion path is a phone number printed as plain text behind a hero button coded href="javascript:;" on a single free-Weebly page last modified 2015-05-21, with no form, hours, booking or schema — https://hugheslaw.weebly.com/ (corroborated by the same attorney's presence on the 2026 NJ Client Protection Fund ineligible list — https://www.njcourts.gov/sites/default/files/attorneys/new-jersey-lawyers-fund-client-protection/ineliglist.pdf)
